headline: This law changes rules for commercial trucks and vehicles using Highway 209 in the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area in Pennsylvania.
what_it_does: It allows smaller commercial vehicles tied to local businesses and residents to use Highway 209 until September 30, 2021. It also directs the Department of the Interior to create a permit and fee program, with an annual fee of up to $200 per vehicle, and to keep those fees in a special account for running the program. School buses, emergency vehicles, and certain commercial vehicles on specified road segments can use the highway without a fee or permit.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses and commercial vehicle owners in the recreation area or nine named nearby Pennsylvania municipalities
who_it_affects.how: Vehicles with four or fewer axles that they own or operate may use Highway 209 under the local business exception until its September 30, 2021 end date.

who_it_affects.group: Commercial vehicle operators who use Highway 209 outside the local business exception
who_it_affects.how: They may need a permit and must pay a fee of up to $200 per year for each vehicle under the new Interior Department program.

who_it_affects.group: Local school districts and school bus operators
who_it_affects.how: Local school buses may use Highway 209 without a fee or permit.

who_it_affects.group: Fire, ambulance, and other emergency service providers
who_it_affects.how: Their safety and emergency vehicles may use Highway 209 without a fee or permit.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of Delaware Township, Dingman Township, Lehman Township, Matamoras Borough, Middle Smithfield Township, Milford Borough, Milford Township, Smithfield Township, and Westfall Township
who_it_affects.how: Commercial vehicles serving residents and businesses in these areas gained a route to use Highway 209 under the local exception.

when_it_takes_effect: Took effect on enactment on January 8, 2018; the local business exception was set to run only until September 30, 2021.
